problem: Reinforcement-learning research in computer audition lacks an open, accessible, audio-only interactive environment; existing embodied-navigation software is vision-centric, and source-separation models are trained on isolated-source/mixture pairs unlike how humans learn.
motivation: Humans learn to parse auditory scenes by moving, investigating sounds and changing how they hear the world. The paper hypothesizes that an agent that learns to locate and turn off sound sources implicitly learns to separate them, and provides a testbed for this.
key_idea: OtoWorld is an audio-only GridWorld-like Gym environment (PyRoomAcoustics RIR simulation) where an agent with two ears must navigate to and 'turn off' sounding sources, with a jointly trained separation network + IPD/ILD spatial features + Q-network baseline.
insight: The agent only slightly beats a random agent (271 vs 409 steps) and is far from the oracle (26 steps), showing audio-only navigation is hard even in a simple anechoic fixed-position setup with dense reward. Separation quality (SI-SIR) can correlate with higher reward but is unstable, with the mixture collapsing into one source after episode 100.
method: Environment: OpenAI Gym + PyRoomAcoustics (shoebox or polygon rooms, absorption/materials) + nussl; random-placed sources with threshold radius, agent with two mics 20 cm apart
Action space: 4 discrete actions (forward, backward, rotate right/left by 30° cumulative); epsilon-greedy with exponentially decaying epsilon
State: at each step a new RIR is computed and the 2-channel time-domain stereo mixture is returned as the observation
Reward: +100 for turning off a source, -0.5 step penalty, optional dense reward based on Euclidean distance to nearest source
Monaural separation model: STFT (256 filter, 64 hop) -> batchnorm -> 1-layer BLSTM with 50 units -> FC softmax producing two masks, applied to each channel
Spatial features: mask-weighted mean IPD and ILD per separated source, concatenated with STFT magnitudes and agent location/orientation

Q-network + training: FC layer with PReLU and softmax over actions; DQN with replay buffer and fixed target network, L1 loss backpropagated through all three components, Adam lr 1e-2, batch 50, 4 s excerpts

setting.backbone: BLSTM separation network + IPD/ILD features + fully-connected Q-network (trained from scratch, DQN)
setting.training_data: Online RL interaction in the simulator; two audio sources (phone ring, police siren); 50 episodes (6x6 m room) and 135 episodes (8x8 m room)
setting.observation: 2-channel (stereo) time-domain audio from two microphones 20 cm apart, plus optional agent location and orientation
setting.action_space: 4 discrete actions: move forward/backward (1.0 m step), rotate left/right 30°
setting.privileged: Agent location and orientation used as optional state; the oracle baseline knows exact source locations (baseline only)

numbers_note: No standard benchmark; results are only average steps per episode (random 409, trained 271, oracle 26) given in text and figures, plus a mean-reward/SI-SIR figure.
results: The trained agent takes 271 steps on average per episode versus 409 for a random agent, and 26 for the oracle, in a simple two-source anechoic setup. Separation is unstable and rewards are low, so this is a preliminary baseline.
limitations: Very simple, preliminary experiment: two stationary sources, fixed positions, anechoic room, dense reward, few episodes
Training is unstable, with separation collapsing into one source and only a slight improvement over a random agent
No standard benchmark or generalization tests; single trial without reported statistics
